subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up + next steps

Thanks for the time today, Alex — quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call.

Recap (what we heard):
- Typical steady-state: ~1.2B tokens / month (est).
- Daily bursts: up to ~5M tokens/day during product launches or campaign spikes.
- Primary concern: predictable unit economics and not getting throttled during bursts.
- Procurement note: looking for a budget range in the $8k–$15k / month band initially.

Pricing notes / qualification we discussed:
- Baseline rate target: you mentioned aiming for roughly $8–$12 per 1M tokens (goal for procurement).
- At $10 / 1M tokens, ~1.2B tokens/mo => ~$12k / month (simple unit-econ calc).
- Key ask: control over quota vs burst capacity and clear overage terms (what happens when you exceed quota).

Rate limit & overage follow-up items:
1) Quota sizing: we should set a daily quota that covers expected steady-state (1.2B/month ≈ 40M/day average) and allow configured burst headroom — recommend an initial quota of 60M/day with bursts up to 5M tokens/day above that for short windows.
2) Burst behavior: we can support short-lived spikes up to your requested burst size; bursts beyond configured burst capacity would either be throttled or billed as overage depending on policy you pick.
3) Overage pricing: typical approach is either a flat per-1M overage rate (e.g., 1.25–1.5x base) or a grace buffer + capped overage for the billing period.
4) SLA & fail-open: we can negotiate an SLA and offer graceful degradation (queueing + fallback models) to avoid hard failures in critical flows.

Next steps (proposed):
- I will send a short pricing sheet that shows (a) list price per 1M tokens, (b) committed discount tiers, and (c) overage math examples.
- Rafael to confirm whether we can offer a trial credit for 30 days to validate burst handling.
- Alex / procurement to confirm target budget range and whether Acme prefers automatic overage billing vs pause/soft-throttle.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up with procurement + engineering to confirm quotas and SLA requirements.

Attaching a preliminary pricing sheet and our rate-limits policy for reference (see attachments).

Thanks 
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

---
Attachment: acme-pricing-sheet-v1.pdf (pricing table + examples)
Attachment: redwood-rate-limits-policy.pdf (burst, quota, overage options)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up + next steps

Thanks — a couple internal notes to align before we send final pricing to Acme: 

1) Pricing bands: we can state list price at $12 / 1M tokens, committed discount tiers: 10% off at $5M/mo commit, 25% off at $20M/mo commit. For short-term motion we can offer a 6-month promotional committed rate of $8 / 1M for a 10M/month committed baseline.
2) Overage policy: propose two options for procurement to choose from:
   - Option A (auto-bill): overage charged at 1.5x base list rate for tokens beyond daily quota in the billing period.
   - Option B (grace + cap): allow up to 20% monthly burst above quota no charge, then overage at 1.25x base up to a hard cap (negotiable).
3) Burst handling: implementation detail — we expose a quota + burst window per customer. Short spikes are allowed by default up to configured burst_capacity (tokens/minute). Anything that exceeds burst_capacity will be throttled unless overage billing is enabled.

I suggest we surface both options to Acme and mark Option B as procurement-friendly. I can approve offering $8/1M for a 6-month committed pilot if they sign an MSA and commit to a minimum of 10M tokens/month.

Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai

From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up + next steps

Thanks, Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- Confirmed volumes: the 1.2B token/month is our baseline estimate (could be +/- 20% depending on campaign cadence). We do expect daily launches with spikes up to ~5M tokens/day for windows of 2–6 hours.
- Budget: procurement is targeting $8k–$14k / month to start; long-term we may expand if the unit economics work.
- Overage handling: procurement preference is Option B — grace + cap. They want to avoid surprise bills. Is there a way to get notification thresholds (email + webhooks) at 70/85/95% of quota?
- Trial: yes, a 30-day trial credit would help validate performance during a campaign spike. Can you confirm any limits in the trial that would affect burst testing?
- SLA: we need a written SLA for availability and an explanation of what happens during sustained over-capacity.

Quick follow-up Q: what is the expected cost at $8 / 1M tokens for our baseline (1.2B tokens)? I want to give procurement a simple number.

Thanks,
Alex Porter
Product Lead, Messaging Platform | Acme Corp
alex.porter@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up + next steps

Alex — great questions. Quick answers + plan: 

1) Cost math at $8 / 1M tokens: 1.2B tokens = 1,200M tokens => 1,200 * $8 = $9,600 / month (simple approximation). I included a small worked example in the attached pricing-sheet.
2) Trial constraints: we can provide a 30-day trial credit that covers up to 50M tokens/day burst testing (should be sufficient to validate your 2–6 hour spikes). We'll include observability hooks so you can see 70/85/95% thresholds and get webhook/email alerts.
3) Overage notifications & policy: we support threshold alerts (70/85/95%) and can hold or auto-bill overage. Based on Rafael's note, Option B (grace + cap) is procurement-friendly — we'll present that as the recommended path. The overage cap is negotiable; typical defaults are 20% free buffer then 1.25x base for the remainder up to a negotiated cap.
4) SLA & sustained over-capacity: SLA will specify availability and latency SLOs; for sustained over-capacity we provide queueing and fallback model options and a documented incident/escalation path.

Next steps / ask list: 
- I will send an updated pricing sheet that includes the $8/1M committed pilot offer, clear overage examples, and the trial credit description (attached).
- Rafael: can you draft the Option B language for the MSA and confirm the 30-day trial credit is approved?
- Alex / Procurement: if the $9.6k/mo at $8/1M looks acceptable, can we schedule a 30-min procurement call next week to review the MSA?

I'll attach the updated pricing sheet and the rate-limits policy for their review. If you want, I can also add an example invoice that shows how overage would appear versus quota.

Thanks!
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
